questions.title: IRCTC / Railway Ticketing System — DB Schema + SQL + Concurrent Booking
questions.body: SSE-2 Round 4 (LeetCode Nov 2023), Tech Lead Round 2 (Jul 2024). Covers: DB schema (trains, stations, routes, seats, bookings), SQL queries to find routes between cities, handling concurrent booking (optimistic locking / SELECT FOR UPDATE), scaling for high traffic.
questions.answer:
Schema key: seat inventory must be per (train, journey_date) (or per schedule run) — a seat booked Monday must stay free Tuesday. Model stops as an ordered list so intermediate-city queries work.

Concurrency: JPA @Version / optimistic locking for low contention. Peak (tatkal): Redis lock with atomic SET seat:lock:{inventoryId} {userId} NX EX 30 (not SETNX+EX as separate commands — that races). Lock → book → release; miss → seat taken.
Scaling: read replicas for availability; writes to primary; partition inventory by train_id; cache popular route counts in Redis (invalidate on booking).

solutions.label: SQL schema

questions.source: Reported: SSE-2 LeetCode Nov 2023, Tech Lead Jul 2024
questions.hint: Key tables: Station, Train, Schedule, Seat, Booking, User. Concurrency: SELECT ... FOR UPDATE on Seat row, or use Redis distributed lock for seat reservation flow.

questions.title: Idempotent Booking + Double Payment Prevention
questions.answer:
Full flow:
1. Client generates UUID idempotencyKey per booking attempt.
2. API: POST /bookings with header Idempotency-Key: uuid.
3. Server atomically SET booking:idem:{key} PROCESSING NX EX 300 in Redis.
4. If key already exists → check if value is DONE:{bookingId} → return cached response (200).
5. Process booking → charge payment → store result as DONE:{bookingId} in Redis with 24h TTL.
6. Also store idempotency_key as UNIQUE column in Booking table — second layer of safety.

For the payment charge itself: Payment gateway also supports idempotency keys. Pass the same key so even if you call the payment gateway twice (network retry), only one charge occurs.

Outbox Pattern (for reliable event publishing): Write booking + outbox event in same DB transaction. Separate poller reads outbox and publishes to Kafka. Guarantees event is published exactly once even if service crashes.
questions.source: Reported: Tech Lead Jul 2024, SDE/SSE-2 Oct 2024 (verbal)

questions.title: URL Shortener / TinyURL — Production Design
questions.body: Senior SDE GFG 2019 + SDE/SSE-2 variant (Oct 2024 — shortened MMT booking URL only accessible by that user). Key additions: API design, DB schema, caching, load balancing, user-specific access control.
questions.answer:
Core design: Auto-increment ID → Base62 encode → ~6–8 char short code (62^6 ≈ 56B codes).

DB: url_mapping(id BIGINT PK AI, short_code VARCHAR(8) UNIQUE, long_url TEXT, user_id BIGINT, expires_at DATETIME, created_at TIMESTAMP)

Redirect: GET /{code} → Redis GET → miss → DB → cache (TTL) → HTTP 302 (prefer 302/307 over 301 so browsers do not permanently cache redirects while you still need analytics / auth / expiry).

Auth variant: JWT → verify url_mapping.user_id → else 403.

Scale: Redirects dominate (think millions–billions/day at large products — size Redis cluster to read QPS, not "100B" as a literal MMT figure). Writes are far smaller; primary + async analytics (Kafka → ClickHouse) is enough. CDN in front helps global latency.
questions.source: Reported: Senior SDE GFG 2019, SDE/SSE-2 Oct 2024
questions.hint: Base62 encoding. Short URL → Redis lookup → DB fallback. Auth: JWT session, short URL tied to userId, validate on redirect.

questions.title: Distributed Cache Design
questions.body: SDE-2 Round 3 (GFG 2021). Design a distributed cache — sharding, consistent hashing, replication, eviction policies, cache coherence in distributed setting.
questions.answer:
Key components:
1. Consistent Hashing: Map keys to nodes on a ring. Adding/removing a node only remaps ~K/N keys (vs. K/2 with simple modulo). Use virtual nodes for uniform distribution.
2. Replication: Each key stored on N nodes (e.g., 3). Reads from any replica. Writes to primary → async replication.
3. Eviction: LRU per shard with max memory limit. TTL expiry (lazy + active background sweep).
4. Cache Coherence: On write, invalidate all replicas (delete-on-write) or use versioned values (read-your-writes consistency).
5. Client-side routing: Clients use the same consistent hash ring to determine which node to contact — no central router bottleneck.

Redis Cluster in production implements this with 16384 hash slots distributed across master nodes, each with replicas.

questions.title: Scalable System for Very High QPS
questions.body: Tech Lead on-site (Jul 2024). General question about architecting for extreme load. Covers: horizontal scaling, stateless services, load balancers (L4/L7), CDN, read replicas, partitioned caches, async processing via message queues.
questions.answer:
Layer by layer approach:
1. Client/CDN: Static assets cached at edge. CDN absorbs 60–70% of traffic before it hits origin.
2. API Gateway: Rate limiting, auth, request routing, SSL termination.
3. Load Balancer: L7 (Application LB) → round-robin / least-connections across stateless service instances. Auto-scaling group expands horizontally.
4. Services: Stateless microservices — no server-side session (JWT). Horizontally scalable.
5. Cache: Redis cluster in front of DB. Cache-aside for hot data. Target 95%+ cache hit rate.
6. DB: Read replicas for 80% read workload. Write to primary. Shard by user_id or booking_id for extreme scale.
7. Async: Non-critical work (emails, analytics, rewards) offloaded to Kafka → workers. Reduces synchronous API latency.
8. Circuit Breakers: Resilience4j on downstream calls. Fallback to stale cache or graceful degradation.
questions.hint: Think in layers: Client → CDN → API Gateway → Service mesh → DB read replicas → async queues. Rate limiting at gateway. Circuit breakers for downstream services.

questions.title: Reducing Latency Between Two Microservices
questions.body: Tech Lead on-site (Jul 2024). Given two services with high latency between them, what are the approaches? Cover: async (Kafka/event), caching (Redis read-through), connection pooling, gRPC instead of REST, co-location, bulk/batch APIs, circuit breakers.
questions.hint: Consistent hashing for key distribution. Each node has replicas. Eviction: LRU or LFU with TTL. Write strategy: write-through for consistency, write-behind for performance.

questions.title: Facebook Messenger / Chat System
questions.body: Naukri Code360 SDE-2 campus (Jul 2022). 1-on-1 + group chat, delivered/read receipts, offline message storage, push notifications, end-to-end encryption, media.
questions.answer: WebSocket for real-time. Fan-out on write for group chat. Message queue (Kafka) for delivery. Cassandra for message storage (wide column, time-series friendly).
questions.hint: WebSocket for real-time. Fan-out on write for group chat. Message queue (Kafka) for delivery. Cassandra for message storage (wide column, time-series friendly).

questions.title: Uber Driver Allocation — LLD of Uber (verbal)
questions.body: CodingKaro SSE/SDE Round 2. Verbal explanation of algorithm to allocate nearest driver + some basic HLD follow-up questions.
questions.answer: Geospatial index (Redis Geo or PostGIS). Driver location updated via Kafka stream. Nearest driver: GEORADIUSBYMEMBER. Assignment: optimistic lock on driver availability flag.
